correctness.rationale: The quiver locus is invariant under the vertex diagonal torus. A generic one-parameter subgroup separates all arrow matrix-coordinate weights, so projective fixed points are coordinate representations. At such a point exactly one direct arrow has rank one and every longer composite is zero, hence membership is equivalent to positivity of that one direct rank bound. The fixed-point count is therefore the stated weighted support sum. Euler localization applies to singular complex algebraic varieties, and projectivity converts compactly supported to ordinary Euler characteristic. The bundled checker independently rebuilds admissible rank arrays from interval modules and re-tests all defining rank inequalities at coordinate points.

value.rationale: Equioriented type-A quiver loci are a central family of singular degeneracy loci linking representation theory, Schubert geometry, and quiver polynomials. The theorem gives a uniform global topological invariant for every admissible rank array and shows a strong structural collapse: all higher composite-rank data, which control codimension and much of the singular geometry, disappear from ordinary Euler characteristic. The ambient-equality corollary applies to every rank array with all direct arrows active, producing broad families of proper singular loci that are Euler-indistinguishable from their ambient projective representation spaces.
